name: Christopher S Kiper
current_role: Co-founder, Managing Director & Chief Investment Officer, Legion Partners Asset Management; director, Lifecore Biomedical (since 2023)
profile: Christopher Kiper co-founded Legion Partners (Los Angeles, 2012), a long-only activist fund targeting North American small caps with fewer than 15 concentrated positions. His wealth tracks Legion's activist stakes, including a 10%+ holding in Lifecore Biomedical, where he sits on the board as Legion's representative. He has also served on boards such as NN Inc.
interesting_fact: Legion describes its method as a 'private equity approach to investing in public equities', running a concentrated book of fewer than 15 small-cap positions and engaging boards directly.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Legion he worked at Shamrock Capital, the Disney family's investment firm. On the Beyond the Boardroom podcast he said 'most boards need upgrading' and that replacing directors is one of the biggest ways to change a company.
notes: Activist investor, not an operator, but a good fit for small-cap governance/value angles. Clear Channel Outdoor's 2024 Legion board seat went to co-founder Ted White, and I could not confirm Kiper sat on the CCO board, so the SEC-derived CCO directorship may be a data error. CCO was later taken private by Mubadala. Reach him through Legion's general inbox.

name: Gerhard Watzinger
current_role: Chairman of the Board, CrowdStrike (since April 2012)
profile: German-born security executive who has chaired CrowdStrike since its 2012 founding. He was CEO of encryption company SafeBoot until McAfee bought it in 2007 for about $350M, then became McAfee's Chief Strategy Officer and EVP. He also sits on the boards of KnowBe4, NinjaOne and Invicti.
interesting_fact: At McAfee he was the architect of the company's $7.7B sale to Intel, before teaming up with McAfee colleagues George Kurtz and Dmitri Alperovitch at CrowdStrike.
deep_cut_fact: He ran SafeBoot, a Dutch-based data-encryption company that McAfee bought for about $350M in 2007, then took over McAfee's new Data Protection business unit and reported to CEO Dave DeWalt. He has an advanced computer-science degree from the University of Applied Sciences in Munich.
notes: Low public profile: he gives few interviews and I found no personal social accounts. The only published route is CrowdStrike corporate communications.

name: Anthony D. Fassino
current_role: Retired Group President, Construction Industries, Caterpillar (retired May 31, 2026); 2025-26 chair of ARTBA
profile: Tony Fassino spent about 30 years at Caterpillar, running Building Construction Products (2018) and then the Construction Industries segment as group president (2021 to early 2026). Earlier he was a senior vice president in the Oil & Gas and Electrification & Energy Solutions divisions. His wealth comes from Caterpillar stock and equity compensation. He handed the segment to Rod Shurman on Feb 1, 2026 and retired May 31, 2026.
interesting_fact: He was elected 2025-26 chair of the American Road & Transportation Builders Association (ARTBA), after several years as a volunteer vice chair. As chair he pushed for practical approaches to Buy America expansion and OSHA's proposed heat rule.
deep_cut_fact: He is a Bradley University mechanical engineer (bachelor's and master's), studying in Peoria, Caterpillar's longtime hometown. Before running construction equipment, he led Cat's Electrification & Energy Solutions division, which is directly relevant to an energy/data-center podcast (Cat gensets power data centers).
notes: Retired from Caterpillar in 2026, so corporate channels may no longer reach him. ARTBA may be a better route while his chair term runs. His energy-solutions background suits the data-center power angle. Some outlets say he joined Cat in 1997 rather than 1996.

name: Sheela Kosaraju
current_role: Executive Vice President & Chief Legal Officer, Ciena Corporation
profile: Sheela Kosaraju has been at Ciena, the optical networking company, since 2010. She rose from international general counsel and head of international legal to SVP & General Counsel (2023), also served as acting Chief People Officer from August 2023, and now signs filings as EVP & Chief Legal Officer. Her wealth is Ciena equity, which has risen sharply as AI data-center bandwidth demand lifted the stock.
interesting_fact: She leads legal at a company now positioned as 'the global leader in high-speed connectivity' for the AI era. In fiscal Q3 2026 two customers made up 41.7% of Ciena's revenue, a sign of how concentrated hyperscaler demand has become.
deep_cut_fact: Before Ciena she was general counsel at two early-stage companies, HomeCom Communications and Closedloop Solutions. For a time she ran Ciena's legal and people (HR) functions at once, as SVP & General Counsel and acting Chief People Officer.
notes: Corporate legal executive with little public profile. Ciena's site blocks automated fetches, so I couldn't confirm a press email; contact Ciena corporate communications through ciena.com. Ciena (optical interconnect for AI data centers) is highly relevant to the podcast's themes. Web search budget ran out at this point, so research relied on SEC filings.

name: Kimberly Alexy
current_role: Founder & principal, Alexy Capital Management; independent director and Audit Committee chair, Western Digital; director, Netskope
profile: Kimberly E. Alexy, a CFA, was an equity research VP at Lehman Brothers (1995-98) and a senior VP and managing director at Prudential Securities (1998-2003). She founded the private investment fund Alexy Capital Management in 2005. She has been a professional public-company director at tech firms including Western Digital (since 2018), Sandisk, Netskope, Five9, Mandiant and Alteryx.
interesting_fact: As Western Digital's Audit Committee chair she leads oversight of the company's enterprise risk management program, at a storage maker now at the center of AI data-center demand. She also served on the board of the spun-off Sandisk.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a finance-trained director, she holds a CERT Certificate in Cybersecurity Oversight for corporate directors, issued by the CERT Division of Carnegie Mellon's Software Engineering Institute. That fits her board seats at security firms Mandiant and Netskope.
notes: Professional board director with a low media profile. The proxy no longer lists Sandisk as a current board, so she appears to have left it. The only published route is through Western Digital IR. Strong fit for a data-storage/AI-infrastructure governance angle.

name: Michael C Ngo
current_role: Chief Innovation Officer, Paysign, Inc. (Nasdaq: PAYS)
profile: Michael Ngo joined Paysign, a prepaid-card and patient-affordability payments company, as Chief Innovation Officer in 2025. Paysign bought substantially all the assets of Gamma Innovation LLC, his blood- and plasma-collection software company, for about $15.6M in total consideration. His holdings come from that deal and from a 2025 restricted-stock grant vesting over five years.
interesting_fact: Paysign closed the Gamma deal in March 2025. It brought a donor-engagement app meant to cut plasma labor costs and donor fees, a CRM for donor retention and marketing, and a donor-management system to make plasma centers more efficient.
deep_cut_fact: Paysign bought Gamma Innovation from him for a $10M cash price paid in five equal annual tranches starting March 19, 2025, plus stock and a $990K earn-out. As a named party to the deal, Ngo became one of Paysign's three named executive officers in his first year.
notes: Little public biography. Identity is confirmed through Paysign filings. Michael Ngo is a common name, so don't attach outside profiles without checking. The SEC-derived $33M figure seems high next to the deal terms and his grants.

name: Assaf Feldman
current_role: Co-founder, director and Chief Strategy Officer - Tech, Riskified (NYSE: RSKD); CTO from founding in 2012 until a 2026 title change
profile: Israeli technologist who co-founded Riskified, an e-commerce fraud-prevention and chargeback-guarantee platform, with Eido Gal. He led its machine-learning risk engine as CTO from inception and took the company public on the NYSE in 2021. He owns about 3.1% of Class A and 20.7% of Class B shares, roughly 17% of the combined voting power.
interesting_fact: He and Eido Gal met at BillGuard, the consumer fraud-alert startup, before leaving to found Riskified. Riskified's filings call their experience building ML-driven risk and identity systems a key asset.
deep_cut_fact: He has a B.A. in Film and Computer Science from Tel Aviv University and an M.A. from MIT, where he was a researcher at the MIT Media Lab (2003-05). Before that he was VP of Engineering at Oddcast, the talking-avatar company, and later lead developer at monitor110.com.
notes: The film-plus-CS background and MIT Media Lab stint make a good conversation opener. Riskified's site and IR pages block automated fetches and I found no published press email in its SEC filings. Use the media form on riskified.com.

name: Mark G Parker
current_role: Executive Chairman of the Board, Nike, Inc.
profile: Mark Parker joined Nike in 1979 as a footwear designer and rose through product development to become its third CEO (2006 to January 2020). He succeeded Phil Knight as chairman in 2016 and has been executive chairman since 2020. He also chaired the Walt Disney Company (2023 until he left its board on Jan 2, 2025). His wealth is decades of Nike equity.
interesting_fact: Fortune named him Businessperson of the Year in 2015. As CEO he kept designing shoes, notably the limited-edition Nike HTM line with Tinker Hatfield and Hiroshi Fujiwara.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Nike's R&D lab in Exeter, New Hampshire, after running track and cross country at Penn State. He collects lowbrow and underground art (Mark Ryden, Todd Schorr, Robert Crumb) and film props, and kept the 'bat-boots' Nike designed for Michael Keaton in the 1989 Batman.
notes: Very high-profile and heavily gatekept; any approach has to go through Nike corporate communications. Wikipedia's lead says his Disney chairmanship ran to 2025, and Disney's 2026 proxy confirms he resigned from its board effective Jan 2, 2025. The SEC 'Disney director' tag is out of date.

name: Derianto Kusuma
current_role: Co-founder of Traveloka (former CTO, stepped down 2018); current role not confirmed
profile: Indonesian software engineer who co-founded Traveloka in 2012 with Ferry Unardi and Albert Zhang. The three met while studying and working in the US. He was CTO when the travel metasearch site launched in September 2012. Traveloka grew into Southeast Asia's largest online travel platform, now headquartered in Singapore. He resigned as CTO in 2018.
interesting_fact: Traveloka started in 2012 as a flight metasearch site built by three Indonesian engineers and became one of Indonesia's first unicorns. It now operates across Thailand, Malaysia, the Philippines, Vietnam, Australia and Japan.
notes: Low public profile since leaving the CTO role in 2018. I couldn't confirm his current activity or alive status in this pass (web search budget exhausted, and Traveloka's site blocked fetches). 'Alive' is set to unknown only because I didn't verify it; I saw no sign of death. Best route is probably via Traveloka corporate communications or a mutual contact in the Indonesian tech ecosystem.

name: Patrick Brown
current_role: Founder of Impossible Foods; professor emeritus of biochemistry, Stanford (current Impossible role not re-verified)
profile: Pat Brown is a Stanford biochemist (MD/PhD, University of Chicago) who invented the DNA microarray and co-founded the Public Library of Science (PLOS). In 2011 he founded Impossible Foods to replace animal agriculture, using heme (soy leghemoglobin) to make plant-based meat taste like beef. He handed the CEO role to Peter McGuinness in 2022; I didn't re-check his current Impossible title in this pass.
interesting_fact: Impossible Foods grew out of an 18-month sabbatical in 2009 that he took to decide how to spend the rest of his career. He concluded that animal-based food production was the world's largest environmental problem.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a pediatrician (three-year residency in Chicago) before switching to basic research. To test his heme hunch early on, he said: 'I dissected them [clover roots] off with a razor blade then blended them up just to see what I could extract.'
notes: Mission-driven scientist-founder who is outspoken and does many interviews, so a good podcast fit (climate, food-system emissions). Impossible's site blocks automated fetches, so I found no press email. Use Impossible's media page manually. The CEO handover year is from background knowledge and wasn't re-verified because the search budget ran out.

name: Achmad Zaky
current_role: Co-founder, Init6 (early-stage venture fund); co-founder and former CEO of Bukalapak
profile: Achmad Zaky, from Sragen in Central Java, co-founded Indonesian e-commerce marketplace Bukalapak in 2010 while just out of Bandung Institute of Technology. He led it as CEO until he resigned in January 2020. Bukalapak later listed in Jakarta and now runs a large warung (small shop) digitisation network. He now backs early-stage startups through Init6, which he co-founded with former Bukalapak CTO Nugroho Herucahyono.
interesting_fact: President Joko Widodo awarded him the Satyalancana Wira Karya in 2016 for exemplary contributions to Indonesia, and EY named him Entrepreneur of the Year (Technology & Digital) in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He taught himself programming from books on a computer his uncle gave him in 1997, and won a national computer-science olympiad in high school in Solo. At ITB he built quick-count election software for a TV station for IDR 1.5 million and ran a noodle business that failed, before starting the consultancy Suitmedia.
notes: Fairly accessible founder-turned-investor and active on Indonesian social media, though I didn't verify his handles in this pass. The failed noodle business is a nice opener. I couldn't reach Init6's website.

name: Andrew Rubin
current_role: Founder, CEO and board member, Illumio
profile: Andrew Rubin founded Illumio, the Zero Trust segmentation and breach-containment cybersecurity company, which reached a multibillion-dollar private valuation. He sets strategy and personally sponsors many of its largest customers, including Citi, HSBC, Salesforce and Microsoft. He is also a board member of Emigrant Bank and an active angel investor in cyber and tech start-ups.
interesting_fact: Goldman Sachs has named him to its '100 Most Intriguing Entrepreneurs' list seven times, and he was EY's Bay Area Entrepreneur of the Year in 2024.
deep_cut_fact: He has a BSBA in Finance from Washington University in St. Louis, where he is a guest lecturer on entrepreneurship and a National Council member of the Skandalaris Center for Entrepreneurial Studies.
notes: Illumio says he 'frequently participates in panels, articles, and podcasts', so he is receptive to podcast invitations. Illumio's news pages list no press email. Use the contact page or reach out through Illumio's PR team.

name: Lucas Pellan
current_role: Co-founder of Sonder (originally Flatbook); current role not confirmed
profile: Lucas Pellan co-founded Flatbook in Montreal in 2014 with Francis Davidson. The company went through the FounderFuel accelerator, was renamed Sonder, and grew into a tech-enabled short-stay apartment and hotel operator valued at over $1B. Sonder shut down in November 2025 and filed for Chapter 7 liquidation after Marriott ended its licensing deal. I couldn't confirm his role or activity since.
interesting_fact: Sonder began in 2014 as Flatbook, a Montreal startup co-founded by Pellan and Francis Davidson, and joined the local FounderFuel accelerator before scaling into a NASDAQ-listed hospitality brand.
notes: Low public profile, and current activity is unknown ('alive' is unknown only because unverified; I saw no sign of death). Sonder no longer exists (shut down Nov 10, 2025; Chapter 7 filed Nov 13, 2025), so there is no corporate route, and outreach shouldn't lean on Sonder's ending. I found no other public contact. The web search budget ran out before I could dig further.

name: Ankit Sobti
profile: Ankit Sobti co-founded Postman, the API development platform that began in 2012 as Abhinav Asthana's side project in Bengaluru. Asthana recruited him and Abhijit Kane, his former Yahoo colleagues, to build the company. As CTO he leads Postman's core technology group. Postman reached a $5.6B valuation in its 2021 Series D and is headquartered in San Francisco.
interesting_fact: Postman's name is a play on the HTTP 'POST' request. The tool grew from a side project into what the company calls the world's leading API platform, still led by all three co-founders.
deep_cut_fact: He started in engineering at Adobe and Yahoo, has a B.E. from Netaji Subhas University of Technology and an MBA from the Indian School of Business, and per Postman's own bio is a Chelsea FC supporter who 'loves his piano, books, beers, and bacon.'
notes: Postman's press page publishes his X and LinkedIn. Postman's AI-agent/MCP tooling fits a data-center/AI-infrastructure conversation. info@postman.com is a general company inbox, not his personal address.

name: Andrew T. Grauer
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Learneo, Inc. (parent of Course Hero, QuillBot, LanguageTool, CliffsNotes, LitCharts, Scribbr, Symbolab)
profile: Andrew Grauer founded Course Hero, the online study platform that reached a multibillion-dollar valuation. He then reorganised it into Learneo, a holding platform of 'builder-driven' learning and productivity businesses including QuillBot, LanguageTool, CliffsNotes, LitCharts, Scribbr and Symbolab. His approach is to 'let CEOs be CEOs': each acquired founder keeps running their own business inside Learneo.
interesting_fact: Learneo runs as a 'fellowship' of founder-CEOs, seven on the platform as of 2023, who stay independent but share learnings and cross-promote products. That is an unusual alternative to a classic roll-up.
deep_cut_fact: Learneo owns CliffsNotes, the study-guide brand that has been trusted by students for more than 60 years, so the founder of a digital study platform now owns the iconic print-era study guide.
notes: The best route is Learneo press. I couldn't fetch the Forbes 2023 profile ('Course Hero Is Graduating—Just In Time') because of a 403. It is linked from Learneo's site and worth reading before outreach.

name: Deng Kangqiao
current_role: Listed by Hurun as a Lalamove (Huolala) founder; role not confirmed
profile: Hurun's unicorn-founder lists name Deng Kangqiao as a founder of Lalamove (货拉拉/Huolala), the Hong Kong-founded on-demand logistics platform now under Lalatech Holdings. English and Chinese Wikipedia credit only Chow Shing-yuk (周胜馥), who started it as EasyVan in December 2013, and I could not confirm Deng's role from an official source.
interesting_fact: Lalamove started in Hong Kong in 2013 as EasyVan and now runs in more than 400 cities across 18 markets. Its parent, Lalatech, calls itself the world's largest logistics transaction platform by closed-loop freight GTV.
notes: Identity is unverified: neither Wikipedia edition mentions him. He may be a co-founder or an early executive named in Lalatech's Hong Kong IPO prospectus, which is worth checking before any outreach. My web search budget was exhausted, so I couldn't search Chinese-language sources. Treat this record as a placeholder.

name: Eric Wilson
current_role: Listed by Hurun as a Better.com founder; role not confirmed
profile: Hurun's unicorn-founder lists include an Eric Wilson as a founder of Better.com, the online mortgage lender now listed on Nasdaq as Better Home & Finance. Wikipedia and Better's SEC filings credit Vishal Garg as the founder (February 2014), and I found no official source confirming Wilson's role. 'Eric Wilson' is a very common name.
interesting_fact: Better was founded after Vishal Garg and his wife ran into long delays buying a home. Garg bought the lender Avex Funding to serve as the operating company for the new digital mortgage business.
notes: Identity is unverified: the name doesn't appear in Better's latest 10-K or on Wikipedia, so he may be an early executive or a Hurun data error. Do not contact on this basis without independent confirmation. Searches were unavailable (budget exhausted).
